children: Suraksha P Bengaluru: The government is exploring an anchor investment of 15,000-20,000 crore for a proposed fund to provide long-term risk capital to India's frontier artificial intelligence companies and finance GPU clusters, specialised data centres and other AI infrastructure.

The proposed National Frontier AI & Compute Fund (NFAICF) under the IndiaAI Mission is still under consultation, and its final size, structure, governance and the role of government capital are yet to be decided, people aware of the discussions told ET. The fund is being designed to attract private capital into frontier AI, as the cost of building models and computing infrastructure is rapidly going beyond the reach of existing Indian venture capital and grant-based funding.

According to a study by research institute Epoch AI, training large frontier models could cost more than $1 billion per run by 2027. "The intent appears to be to explore a 50:50 model with private participation," K Bhaskar Varma, chief business officer at NxtGen Datacenter & Cloud Technologies, said, noting the cost involved in building large-scale AI infrastructure.

While the IndiaAI Mission offers access to subsidised compute and funding for indigenous foundation models through its 10,372-crore outlay, the government noted that there is currently no dedicated domestic equity vehicle to support frontier AI development. The proposed NFAICF was discussed at a closed-door meeting on 'Financing India's Frontier & Compute Ecosystem' in Delhi on Thursday.

Several AI startups and ecosystem stakeholders, including Vivek Raghavan, cofounder of Sarvam AI, Peak XV managing director Rajan Anandan, Tarun Dua, chief executive of E2E Networks, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology secretary S Krishnan and officials of the IndiaAI Mission, attended the meeting.

The meeting was primarily aimed at gathering views from venture capital firms, infrastructure providers and other stakeholders on the role the government could play as a catalyst for frontier AI, Varma said. "They were exploring what kind of financing models could be put in place to give an impetus to the AI sector," he said. The discussions also examined how private capital could be brought into the proposed fund and whether international institutions such as the International Finance Corporation could play a role, Varma added. "Initiatives of this kind are essential to India's AI ambitions and should move swiftly from consultation to implementation," said Anuj Bairathi, chief executive of Cyfuture, one of the 14 empanelled cloud service providers of IndiaAI Mission.

title: Govt Eyes Rs 20kcr Fund to Power Up Frontier AI and Compute Ecosystem
